title: Wodehouse - the Romance Of An Ugly Policeman

cognitive_validation.rationale: With no novum present, there is no imaginary science or systematic estranging social organization to validate cognitively.

novum_candidates.description: The candidate elements in this Wodehouse story are the mundane social world of Battersea Park Road, an ugly policeman's unrequited love, the milkman rival, and the petty-theft arrest that ends with the constable offering to sacrifice his career. None of these constitutes a novum.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No cognitive estrangement is generated; the reader recognizes a familiar realist milieu with no departure from the empirical world.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The narrative is governed by realistic romantic and moral drama, not by any novel invention or world-altering premise. No candidate device dictates the story logic in an estranging way.

novelty.rationale: The story presents an ordinary early-twentieth-century London setting with policemen, milkmen, cooks, and flats. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm; the storyworld is the author's own contemporary reality.
